The script's character note says the stick is 'in her hand from the dismount in 2.2 onward', and the closing notes repeat the handover. On the page, the stick first appears in 2.3, already in her hand. The unlettered frame (chapters/ch09-split/frames/page-02-panel-02-v01.png) is a wide 3:2 image and does show the beat. Padmini stands beside the dark horse with one hand on the saddle and the walking stick in her other hand. So the art is correct, and the problem comes from page layout and lettering. The page crops the wide frame into a roughly 1.18:1 half-width panel, and the second balloon sits right on the action. This fits the brief's 'major' category (a crop or balloon hiding the action). It is not a blocker: no redraw is needed, the panel still reads as an arrival, and 2.3 carries the stick on. Fix: move or shrink the second balloon, for example into the sky or wall area on the left, or into the space above the clerk, or widen the panel so the scripted 'Wide' framing comes through. The secondary claims are too slight to count. The clerk wears a white upper cloth and the swordsman a cloth over one shoulder, both with white mundus. That is a plausible Nair variant, and the continuity bible does not forbid it. The clerk is visibly not Ramayyan (round face, greying moustache, palm-leaf bundle), as the script asks. Their gaze, toward the left or the riders rather than an empty doorway, is a polish-level difference.

confirmed.description: The physical beat is missing. The script asks for a low angle with Revathi's finger pointing down at the verandah stone between the two mats, large in frame. verdict.reason: The claim holds, but it is minor, not major. I zoomed into page-07.png at about x150-918, y358-1198. Panel 7.1 is an eye-level medium two-shot, not a low angle. Revathi's near hand rests on her knee at about (180-260, 700-800). Her far forearm, with the bangle, crosses her lap and its hand goes behind the tail of the "Not to my husband..." balloon. Nothing in the panel points at the verandah stone, and nothing about her hands is large in frame, so the gesture the script calls for in 7.1 is not there. The story beat still comes through, though. Both dialogue lines are present and readable. Revathi leans forward with her eyes down at the floor between the mats. A large foreground stone step and the red courtyard earth just past it fill the lower part of the panel, so "This land" still has something to point to. A reader without the script would see nothing wrong. This is a missed staging touch that weakens the panel, not a missing beat, a wrong identity or a broken panel, so it does not have to be redrawn before publication. Optional polish: redraw with her finger pressed to the stone between the mats, and move the long balloon higher or to the right so the stone stays visible.

confirmed.description: The wordless 'Wide and still... hold the silence a beat too long' panel is a small centred strip, roughly a thumbnail, with blank page on both sides. It has none of the weight the held silence needs, and the motionless banners are absent.

verdict.reason: Confirmed, and the measurements back it up. On page-07.png (1838 px wide, 300 DPI), panel 7.5 spans x619 to x1217 and is about 250 px tall. The rows above use the full live area, x148 to x1688. DPI-REPORT.json has page-07-panel-05 clipped to 142.9 x 59 pt, which is about 2.0 x 0.82 inches. That leaves about 1.6 inches of blank cream on each side. Other single-tier panels in the chapter are placed full width: 10.5 at 350.6 pt and 1.5 at 350.6 pt. LAYOUT-fitted-s1m.json gives page 7 row 3 only 59 pt. The 3:2 source (1536x1024) was fitted to that height, so the panel shrank to a centred thumbnail. This is a leftover from the fitting step, not a framing choice. The script asks for "Wide and still... Hold the silence a beat too long", but at print size the seated figures are about 0.6 inch tall and their faces are only a few millimetres across, so the beat has no weight. The content is all there: both figures on separate mats with a gap between them, and plates of rice barely touched. So this is not a missing beat or a blocker. It is a localized layout and crop problem that weakens the chapter's key silent beat, so major is the right severity. The fix is to give row 3 more height or use a full-width banner crop like 1.5 and 10.5. The missing banners matter less: none appear on this verandah in 7.1 to 7.4 either, so that point alone would be minor.

confirmed.description: The imagined Nashik bleed reads as a literal view from the verandah rather than an image bleeding in behind him. The grey basalt mesas sit beyond a pillar, with the full-colour red courtyard, a wall and foliage in front of them. The jowar fields, the subject of the caption 'my own family fields', are mostly under the caption box. The smoke is a tall, dark plume rather than a single thin column just beginning to rise.
confirmed.evidence: page-08.png, panel at about y2110-2545. The mesas are at about x1000-1680, y2220-2300. The red-earth courtyard and wall in full colour are at about x1000-1680, y2440-2530. The caption box at about x870-1480, y2280-2445 covers the fields. The smoke column is at about x1500-1560, y2140-2280.

verdict.reason: Partly confirmed, but it is minor, not major. Page 8, panel 8.5 does stage the Nashik image as a view from the verandah. The grey mesas and sky sit behind the stone pillar (about x1000-1100 at full resolution). The low wall, the red courtyard (about y2440-2530) and the green-yellow foliage in front are all in full colour. The script asks for a soft-edged image bleeding in behind him, and the page 6 panel 6.4 ledger bleed (smoky sepia edges) shows that device clearly, but this panel does not. The smoke (about x1500-1560, y2140-2280) is one column, thin at the base. But it is a full plume reaching the top of the panel, not one "just beginning to rise", so it reads closer to fields already burning than the script wants. The claim that the fields are mostly hidden is overstated: the caption covers the middle, but standing jowar with clear seed heads is plain at the right (about x1490-1680, y2330-2420). The beat still reads, because the strong grey wash sets the Deccan landscape apart from the colour foreground, and the caption names the Nashik fields. So this is a polish fix, not a clearly wrong panel. Suggested fix: soften or vignette the edge of the grey image so it bleeds in behind Nagoji, not past the courtyard, and shorten the smoke to a thin wisp at the horizon.

confirmed.description: Callback mismatch. The insert under 'your feet are already on the path' shows tall knee-high riding boots, but the boots Nagoji set on the step in 2.4 (and that return in 12.1) are short lace-up ankle boots. The 'Do not pretend...' balloon also covers the boots' feet where they stand on the step.
confirmed.evidence: page-09.png, panel at about x922-1690, y360-1130: knee-high boots at about x1180-1405, y575-890. Compare page-02.png 2.4 (lace-up ankle boots at about x335-500, y1945-2065) and page-12.png 12.1 (lace-up ankle boots at about x300-470, y1035-1200).

verdict.reason: I confirm this one. In the page-09.png crop at x922-1690, y360-1130, panel 9.2 shows a pair of plain, pull-on, knee-high leather riding boots with no laces. The same boots appear elsewhere as a different design. In page-02.png 2.4 (about x335-500, y1945-2065) and page-12.png 12.1 (about x300-470, y1035-1200), the boots on the step are short, laced ankle or lower-calf boots with visible eyelets and laces. The V13 nagoji-v2 commander sheet also shows laced, wrapped mid-calf boots, so 9.2 matches neither the sheet nor its own callbacks. The script says the 9.2 insert shows "His boots standing side by side on the verandah step where he left them". Its notes treat the boots left at the step in 2.4 as the "path" image that returns in 11.3 and 12.1. The bible lists only "boots" for Nagoji with no permission to vary them. So nothing in the script or bible allows a different pair. This is not a small difference that disappears at print size. The boots are the only subject of a half-width insert, and their height and laces read clearly. A reader looking for the callback sees a different pair of boots. The second point holds but is minor: the "Do not pretend..." balloon covers the foot and toe of the right boot, though the left boot's sole is still visible on the step, so the image still reads. I rate this major, not blocker. It is a prop continuity error confined to one panel, and the beat (boots left on the step under "your feet are already on the path") still comes across. The fix is to redraw 9.2 with the laced ankle boots from 2.4 and 12.1 and move the bottom balloon so it no longer covers the foot.

refuted.description: Revathi touches him. Her fingers rest on Nagoji's bared forearm, although the script says 'Nothing is touched' on page 12. The contact spends the near-touch in 12.4 before that panel can land.
refuted.reason: Refuted. I zoomed panel 12.3 on page 12 at full resolution (crop around x 490-540, y 1920-1980 of the 1838x2775 render). Her hand with the bangles does not touch his forearm. The dark verandah background shows clearly between her index and middle fingertips and the upper edge of his bared left forearm, a gap of about 4 to 6 px at 300 DPI. Her ring and little fingertips are not over his arm at all. They lie over her own other forearm, which hangs down behind his wrist. Her fingers also sit at the elbow end of his forearm, outside the brand and scar area, not "just above the scar" as the reviewer said. His fingers curled below the palm belong to his own hand, not hers. So the art shows a hand reaching close to the arm with a gap, not contact, and "Nothing is touched" holds. 12.4 still plays the real near-touch: her fingertip hovers over his wrist and palm. At print size 12.3 reads as nearly touching, so it slightly anticipates 12.4. That is a matter of taste, not the reported error.

refuted.description: The servant's tail points to Nagoji, not the servant. 'The Velinadu lady asks if your feet remember her verandah.' therefore reads as Nagoji's line.
refuted.reason: I measured the art and it does not support the claim. On page 11, panel 11.5, I traced the tail's white interior in the 300 DPI render. The tip is at about original (970,1980), which is display (840,1430). The axis runs from the base midpoint up and to the left, with a slope of about -0.56 px in x per px in y. Extended, that axis passes straight through the servant's cupped hand and mouth. I checked this by drawing the extended axis onto a zoomed crop. The tail points away from Nagoji's face, which is up and to the right of the tip. The tip is about 64 original px (about 5 mm at print size) short of the servant's mouth, and about 100 px from Nagoji's mouth. It is closer to the servant's mouth and aimed at it. It only stops on Nagoji's near sleeve because his arm sits between the balloon and the servant. The evidence's statement that the tail "does not point toward" the servant's mouth is wrong. The context also settles the speaker. The servant is drawn whispering with his hand cupped at his mouth, leaning toward Nagoji. The line ("asks if your feet remember her verandah") is plainly a message delivered to Nagoji, and Nagoji could not say it. This matches the script: 11.5 has SERVANT speaking, and the servant is leaning in toward Nagoji. A reader will not take it as Nagoji's line. One optional polish change: lengthen the tail about 40 to 60 px up and to the left, so the tip clears Nagoji's sleeve and ends near the servant's hand. That is cosmetic, not a misattribution.

refuted.description: Padmini's 'They will make you wait. That is part of the weighing.' balloon sits across Nagoji's chest directly under his face. Its tail is a tiny nub tucked against the caption box, so the line reads as Nagoji's. Nagoji's turban is also cut off by the panel's top border.
refuted.reason: Refuted as a major problem. I zoomed in on page 2, panel 2.4 (original pixels about x971-1151, y1692-1831). The tail is a clear, properly outlined wedge on the balloon's right edge. Its tip ends at Padmini's neck and jaw, just under her chin, at about original (1120,1720). It does not stop at the caption box, and it points away from Nagoji. Nothing on the balloon's upper or left edge points toward Nagoji. At reduced, near-print size the wedge is still visible and plainly aims at Padmini, whose face is turned toward Nagoji just beside it. The line also fits the context: she is the insider explaining the court's custom, as the script gives it (PADMINI in 2.4). It does not read as Nagoji speaking. The balloon does sit over Nagoji's chest, and the tail is short (about 40 px, roughly 0.13 in at 300 DPI), so a longer tail would be good optional polish. That is not a misattribution. The turban crop is also slight: only the top of the crown touches the top border, while his face, moustache and most of the red turban stay fully visible. That is normal framing for a seated two-shot and does not hide any action. No redraw is needed.

refuted.description: In this over-the-shoulder shot, Revathi's 'He builds a state that answers to the crown...' balloon sits on Nagoji's back and shoulder, and its tail stops on the pillar short of her. The line can be misread as Nagoji's. The script's instruction to 'Stack the balloons down one side and keep both heads clear' is not followed: the balloons are spread top, left and bottom-right.
refuted.reason: I checked page 7, panel 7.3 at full resolution (crop x145-920, y1200-2295, with the tail zoomed 2x). The balloon does overlap Nagoji's tunic, and its tail tip stops on the stone pillar. But the tail points up and to the right, at Revathi's shoulder and face, and away from Nagoji. His head is above and to the left of the balloon, and his back is to the camera, so his mouth is not shown. The gap between the tip and Revathi's shoulder is about 55 px at 300 DPI, roughly 4-5 mm, with the tail aimed straight at her. Tails that stop short of the speaker are standard practice. The text also continues her 'Your king...' line, and she is the only speaker in the panel. A real misattribution to Nagoji is unlikely. The script asks to 'keep both heads clear', and both heads are fully clear: the top balloon sits above Revathi's head and the left balloon sits below Nagoji's turban and face. The balloons are not 'stacked down one side'. However, the reading order still works: top-right first, then the left balloon (top at y~1755), then bottom-right (top at y~1900). Nothing is hidden or out of order, so this layout difference does not cause a lettering defect at print size. At most it is optional polish: extending the middle tail past the pillar to touch Revathi would make it airtight.

refuted.description: Panel widths are ragged throughout. Many panels are inset by different amounts, so the left and right page margins zigzag from row to row. The approved Ch1 page 1 keeps every panel on one 148-1688 px margin, so these pages do not read as clean comic pages.
refuted.reason: The measurements are correct, but the claim that this breaks the approved standard is wrong. I re-measured the panel x-extents and got the reviewer's numbers: Ch9 p1 187-1650, 359-1477, 148-1688 and so on; p2 352-1485, 148-1688, 308-1528, 420-1417; p10, p12, 6.5 and 11.1 as stated. The comparison only holds for Chapter 1 page 1. The rest of the approved Chapter 1 has the same zigzag, and it is identical in every round from r3 to r6. Ch1 p6 runs 148-1688, 207-1630, 414-1422, 261-1575, 148-1688. Ch1 p8 runs 148-1688, 148-1688, 211-1626, 148-1688, 234-1603. Ch1 p2, p3, p4, p5 and p7 also have inset rows. Later chapters show the same pattern: Ch2 r4 p1 (207-1629, then three rows at 318-1519), Ch3 r9 p3 and p8 (461-1376), Ch5-split r2 p7 (433-1404, 466-1371) and Ch6 r6 p8 (516-1320). The insets come from the documented compositor policy in pipeline/README.md. It keeps the aspect ratio and the visible crop, and it says outright that many panels come out narrower than the column. The fit only tries to keep this small, and the book's earlier rounds accepted the moderate centred insets that result. The narrowest Ch9 rows the reviewer cites (6.5 at 1077 px, 11.1 at 875 px) are within that precedent (Ch6 p8 is 804 px, Ch1 p6 is 1008 px). At print size these pages read as centred inset tiers, the same as the approved chapters. The "Ch1 keeps one 148-1688 margin" standard does not exist, so this is house style, not a defect.

refuted.description: The script has Padmini looking toward the doorway Revathi went through. In the render she is a sliver cropped at the left frame edge, turned and looking out of frame to the left, away from the open doorway on the right. Two balloons cover most of her body, so the panel shows an empty verandah and door with no one looking at it.

In a zoomed crop of page-11.png at about x140-420, y900-1150, Padmini's head is turned three-quarters toward frame-right, not frame-left. Her eyes, brow and nose all point right, across the verandah toward the open doorway at about x620-900, so the beat "Padmini, looking toward the doorway where Revathi went" reads correctly. She sits at the left edge of the frame, but her face, earring, necklace and saree are fully visible. The second balloon covers her torso and leaves her face clear. The door, the lamp-lit inner room and the mat are clearly drawn, so the panel shows her looking at the empty doorway, which is what the script asks for. The first balloon does sit partly across her line of sight to the door. That is a small layout preference, not a fidelity error, and it doesn't hide the action at print size.

refuted.description: The script beat is Nagoji 'looking away from her for the first time, out at the courtyard'. In the render he looks to frame-left, which is where Revathi's off-panel tails come from in 9.2 and where she sits in 9.4, while the courtyard is behind him to the right. The art reads as him looking at her, which inverts the beat.
refuted.reason: I zoomed in on Nagoji's head in panel 9.3 (page-09.png, about x370-480, y1210-1290), and he is not looking frame-left. His face is drawn three-quarter, turned toward frame-right. The ear with the stud is on the frame-left side of his head, and the nose and moustache profile stick out on the frame-right side. His pupils sit in the right-hand corners of his eyes, so his gaze runs frame-right. That puts it past the pillar toward the trees, the courtyard wall and the red earth on the right side of the panel (about x620-910). The reviewer's own evidence places Revathi to frame-left: the 9.2 tails meet at the left edge, and she sits frame-left in 9.4. So he is looking away from her and out at the courtyard, which is exactly the script beat for 9.3 ("looking away from her for the first time, out at the courtyard"). Panel 9.4 matches too: Nagoji's eyes again go frame-right, away from Revathi on the left. The reviewer misread the direction of his head turn, and the beat is not inverted.

minors.description: In the brand insert, the off-panel tails run as long wedges across the subject. 'A brand. Some scars...' cuts across his fist and the pushed-up sleeve to the top-left corner. minors.evidence: Crop of display x660-1220, y255-975: the left tail runs from about (835,700) to (675,270) over the hand. The right tail runs from about (1090,765) to (1210,510) across the forearm's edge beside the brand (brand at about 1080-1170, 590-680).

minors.description: Nagoji's face is jammed against the top border and hemmed in by three balloons. 'I have seen their hunger.' butts up against the tip of his moustache, and the turban is cut off by the panel's top edge.
minors.evidence: Crop of display y1310-1595: the 'I have seen their hunger' balloon's left edge (about x545) meets the moustache tip (about x540, y1360). 'Because in Goa' and 'Give them an inch' sit on either side of and below his face.

minors.description: Several balloons and one caption are set as tall, narrow columns of one to three words per line, which read choppily and unlike the wide captions and balloons in the approved Ch1. 8.2 ('You fear / he will use / men like / me to cut / your / houses / down.') also touches the top border.
minors.evidence: 8.2 Nagoji balloon: 7 lines, display x920-1095, top at y~262 against the 260 border. 1.1 caption: 6 lines ('Padmini / Amma / was / taking / me to be / weighed.'). 7.4 'She writes to me...': 7 lines. 8.4 'If he tells you...': 6 lines. 12.1 'You heard many words...': 5 lines.

minors.description: The tail of Revathi's opening balloon, 'You heard many words today...', ends on a brass lamp in the doorway, about 200 px short of her head. The tail of 'Not bad...' ends at her sari hem. Both point in the right general direction, but neither reaches the speaker.
minors.evidence: 'You heard' tail tip at display about (275,450), with Revathi's head at about (400,290). 'Not bad' tail tip at about (440,690), at the hem of her sari.

minors.description: The caption 'The words were light. The tone was not.' is set almost on the panel's right border, which reads as a doubled line. Captions in the approved Ch1 sit inset from the borders.
minors.evidence: Zoomed crop of display x990-1225, y255-360: the caption's right edge and the panel border run about 5 px apart as two parallel black lines, and the caption's top is flush with the panel top.

minors.description: Revathi's 'So you chose him.' balloon sits directly under Nagoji's chin, covering his neck. The tail correctly points left to Revathi, but its placement next to his mouth invites a misread.
minors.evidence: Balloon at display about x830-1040, y945-1030. Nagoji's chin is at about (965,940), and the tail tip at about (820,960) is on Revathi's shoulder.

minors.description: The script gives 12.3 only Revathi's gaze dropping to the scar. In the render her hand is already raised with her fingers at his forearm. That pre-empts the 12.4 near-touch, and at this size it can read as an actual touch on a page where 'Nothing is touched'.
minors.evidence: page-12.png, panel at about x150-918, y1625-2070. Her fingers are at about (470-520,1925-1945), directly on the top edge of his bared forearm at about (480-560,1945-1990).

minors.description: The servant wears a long-sleeved white shirt and a white head-wrap, where the script and the Nair standing note call for a plain white mundu with no turban. Padmini stands alone in the doorway facing out, rather than talking quietly with the house elders.
minors.evidence: page-11.png: the servant is at about x925-1110, y1820-2380, with the head-wrap at about (1050-1100,1830-1870). Padmini faces the viewer at about x1420-1550, y1830-2230, with the elders behind her at about x1550-1690.

minors.description: 'Not from mine' (kept verbatim for the chapter 20 payoff) is staged as a medium seated shot. The script asks for a tight shot of her bare right shoulder lifting in a small shrug. Her shoulders are level, and there is no shrug.
minors.evidence: page-10.png, panel at about x150-918, y360-925. Revathi is at waist-up medium scale, with her hands resting on her knees at about (480-640,780-910).

minors.description: Prop continuity. Revathi pushes aside a brass plate that is empty and polished, although the plate is 'barely touched' with food on it in 6.1 and 7.5. A stray pebble sits beside it.
minors.evidence: page-08.png, panel at about x150-918, y1130-2045: an empty plate at about (580-910,1820-1910). Compare page-07.png 7.5, where both plates hold rice at about (870-1000,2480-2530) and (1150-1300,2480-2530).

minors.description: The script asks for a panel 'Taller than the other panels' with the balloons stacked down one side. The render is the same height as 7.4, the balloons are split across both sides, and 'That is good for facing Europeans...' sits over Revathi's torso.
minors.evidence: page-07.png: 7.3 at about x150-918, y1204-2288 has the same height as 7.4 at x922-1690. Balloons sit at upper centre (about x500-900, y1240-1525), at left (about x150-510, y1760-1980) and at lower centre (about x540-890, y1920-2280).

minors.description: The doorway shows lit, solid seated women rather than shadows on a lamp-lit inner wall. The shot is a side-by-side two-shot, not 'from beside Revathi, past Nagoji's shoulder'.
minors.evidence: page-09.png, panel at about x922-1690, y1140-1745: seated figures in the doorway at about x1500-1640, y1270-1370. Revathi and Nagoji are both facing camera at about x930-1150 and x1210-1560.

minors.description: The foreground figure carrying 'Go.' is almost entirely hidden. Revathi's 'hand dropped, already half turned away' cannot be seen under her balloon and the first caption, and only her face shows.
minors.evidence: page-12.png, panel at about y2075-2545. Revathi's face is at about x370-490, y2085-2200. The balloon at about x150-800, y2205-2385 and the caption at about x150-705, y2400-2525 cover the rest of her.

minors.description: Rider blocking does not follow the script. Padmini is not clearly at the head, and Nagoji rides level with her on her right (frame left), where the script places him a little behind and to her left. 1.3 then frames the riding two-shot between two gate pillars, so the mid-ride conversation looks like another gate arrival.
minors.evidence: page-01.png, 1.1 at about y360-680: Nagoji is at about x560-780 and Padmini at about x910-1130, at the same depth. 1.3 has gate pillars at the left (about x220-320, y1220-1800) and the right (about x1610-1690, y1220-1800).

minors.description: Nagoji's reply 'I learn it. Slowly...' has its tail aimed at an unidentifiable brown shape in the lower-right corner. It does not read as Nagoji, who wears a cream tunic.
minors.evidence: page-04.png: the tail tip is at about (1630,670), and the brown blob is at about x1420-1690, y760-890.

minors.description: The script asks for a full-width panel on 'Nagoji's face, hard'. His turban is cut by the top frame line, and his face is wedged between three balloons, one of which butts against his mouth.
minors.evidence: page-06.png, panel at about y1825-2210. His head is at about x600-760, y1825-1945, with the turban cropped at y1825. 'I have seen their hunger.' at about x760-1125, y1830-1950 touches his moustache.
